paragraphs: Class-incremental learning asks a model to learn new categories over time while retaining useful behavior on earlier ones. Analytic learning makes these updates efficient by using recursive, closed-form calculations. This paper studies why that approach can become unreliable with pretrained models and identifies rigid representations as the main bottleneck: efficient updates cannot fully compensate when the features do not adapt appropriately.

VILA addresses this problem through two branches and two levels of calibration. At the feature level, it geometrically aligns and combines adaptable, task-specific features with a frozen visual representation that supplies a stable reference. At the decision level, it uses semantic information connecting vision and language to correct prediction bias.

The approach matters because it addresses both the representation being updated and the decisions made from that representation. Across eight benchmarks, the authors report consistently superior performance, with particular strengths on fine-grained categories and long sequences of learning tasks. These findings support combining adaptable features with stable visual and semantic references while preserving the efficiency of analytic updates.
icml-2026-advancing-analytic-class-incre.tldr: VILA combines adaptable visual features, a frozen visual reference, and language-based calibration to improve efficient class-incremental learning.

paragraphs: Generating formally verified code requires producing a program whose correctness can be established against a precise specification. Comparing models across verification languages has been difficult because existing benchmarks use different tasks. AlgoVeri addresses this by evaluating the same 77 classical algorithms in Dafny, Verus, and Lean, with identical functional contracts defining the required behavior.

This alignment exposes differences that aggregate coding scores can hide. The abstract reports 40.3% success for Gemini-3 Flash in Dafny, alongside lower figures of 24.7% in Verus and 7.8% in Lean. Dafny offers high-level abstractions and automated reasoning, while Verus adds systems-level memory requirements and Lean demands explicit proof construction.

The study also examines whether repeated repair attempts help. Gemini-3 benefits substantially, including tripling its Dafny pass rate, whereas GPT-OSS levels off early. Error analysis suggests that the verification language shapes what models struggle to repair: logical correctness in Dafny, and persistent syntactic and semantic obstacles in Verus and Lean. The benchmark therefore measures both task success and the different demands of verification workflows.
icml-2026-algoveri-an-aligned-benchmark-.tldr: AlgoVeri aligns 77 algorithm tasks across three verification languages, revealing substantial differences in model success and iterative repair.

paragraphs: An autonomous agent's memory must retain more than a conversation. Over a long task, the agent encounters states, takes actions, receives observations, and reads tool outputs. AMA-Bench evaluates memory using these interaction histories, addressing a mismatch between dialogue-focused benchmarks and the information agents actually need to preserve.

The benchmark combines two sources of evidence. Real application trajectories come with questions curated by experts, while synthetic trajectories can extend to arbitrary lengths and support questions generated from rules. This combination allows evaluation on realistic histories as well as controlled histories whose length can be increased.

The authors find that existing memory systems struggle to preserve causal and objective information and depend heavily on similarity retrieval that loses relevant content. Their proposed AMA-Agent constructs causality graphs and retrieves information with tool support. It achieves 57.22% accuracy, reported as outperforming the strongest baseline by 11.16%. The result supports organizing memory around relationships within an agent's experience, beyond retrieving fragments that merely resemble a question.
icml-2026-ama-bench-evaluating-long-hori.tldr: AMA-Bench tests memory over extended agent interactions, and AMA-Agent improves results using causality graphs and tool-assisted retrieval.

paragraphs: Inverse microstructure design starts with desired physical behavior and searches for a structure that produces it. The challenge grows when several kinds of physics interact. The paper describes traditional topology optimization as often too computationally demanding, while deep generative approaches can propose structures whose apparent suitability is unsupported by their physical behavior.

AutoMS divides the work between language-driven coordination and simulation-grounded numerical search. Language models interpret complex requirements, break them into parts, and coordinate multiple agents. A Simulation-Aware Evolutionary Search component handles numerical optimization through local gradient approximations and directed parameter updates. This gives semantic planning and physical optimization distinct responsibilities.

Across 17 cross-physics tasks, AutoMS achieves a reported state-of-the-art success rate of 83.8%, outperforming traditional evolutionary algorithms and existing agentic baselines. The findings support the framework's division of labor: language models guide the search at a high level, while numerical updates remain tied to simulation. Its contribution is a way to connect flexible requirement interpretation with optimization over complex physical design spaces.
icml-2026-automs-multi-agent-evolutionar.tldr: AutoMS combines language-model coordination with simulation-aware evolutionary optimization, reporting 83.8% success across 17 cross-physics design tasks.

paragraphs: Scene graph generation describes objects and their relationships in an image. This paper focuses on a consistency problem: a model may describe a relationship from the subject's perspective but fail to give a logically compatible description when attention shifts to the object. The authors attribute this to treating relationships mainly as one-way mappings.

Their Mutual-Perspective Inverse Relations principle requires compatible interpretations across the two perspectives. Reciprocal Perspective Calibration turns that principle into a model-agnostic framework using adaptive inverse-relation augmentation. It also introduces prompts guided by broader semantic categories to help vision-language models represent inverse relationships while balancing semantic context and computational efficiency.

Experiments show competitive performance on standard scene graph benchmarks and a significant improvement in understanding inverse relations under a new inverse-consistency evaluation protocol. These are related but distinct findings: ordinary benchmark performance remains competitive, while the targeted consistency capability improves. The work highlights that recognizing a relationship also involves keeping its meaning coherent when the direction of description changes.
icml-2026-beyond-unidirectional-bias-rec.tldr: Reciprocal Perspective Calibration improves scene graph models' ability to describe relationships consistently from both subject and object perspectives.

paragraphs: Direct Preference Optimization can train a language model to recommend items in ways that match historical user behavior. The paper finds that this alignment can also strengthen misleading associations created by the environment in which the behavior was recorded. When that environment changes, recommendations based on those associations can generalize poorly.

CausalDPO extends preference optimization with mechanisms intended to recover more stable preferences. It uses backdoor adjustment during alignment to address environmental confounding, soft clustering to represent an unobserved distribution of environments, and invariance constraints to encourage consistency across them. Together, these components seek to separate enduring preference structure from environment-dependent patterns.

The theoretical analysis supports CausalDPO's ability to capture stable preferences across multiple environments. Experiments cover four representative distribution-shift settings and report an average performance improvement of 24.10% across four evaluation metrics. The findings suggest that matching historical preferences becomes more robust when the training objective also accounts for how the environment shaped the observed behavior, rather than treating every observed association as equally dependable.
icml-2026-causal-direct-preference-optim.tldr: CausalDPO adds environmental adjustment and invariance constraints to preference optimization to improve recommendation robustness under distribution shifts.

paragraphs: A classifier can make correct predictions by relying on incidental patterns that stop working in a different setting. Many approaches counter these spurious correlations by balancing predefined groups, but identifying those groups requires bias annotations or predictions. This paper instead frames the problem as a mismatch between class-conditional distributions caused by biases that need not have an interpretable meaning.

The proposed method reweights training examples to balance those distributions. Its objective is to increase uncertainty about the label when only spurious factors are available. In plain terms, the method seeks a weighted dataset in which misleading factors provide less useful information about which class an example belongs to.

The reweighting automatically emphasizes minority groups and classes while mitigating the need to annotate or predict biases. Experiments and analysis show consistently strong overall performance and results competitive with methods that use bias supervision. The contribution is a distribution-balancing route to robustness that can address general biases without first requiring a human-readable account of each one.
icml-2026-class-conditional-distribution.tldr: The paper improves robust classification by reweighting examples to balance class-conditional distributions without requiring explicit bias labels or predictions.

paragraphs: Supervised fine-tuning trains language models to reproduce the tokens in expert demonstrations. For reasoning, however, success depends on valid logic or a correct outcome, and multiple wordings may express the same reasoning. This paper investigates whether forcing a close fit to every demonstration token can pull training away from that underlying goal.

The authors observe that tokens assigned low probability often reflect stylistic choices or particular ways of expressing an answer. Reducing their influence improves generalization in the reported reasoning experiments. Based on this observation, Bounded Log-Likelihood Loss limits the gradient contribution of low-probability tokens while retaining conventional optimization behavior elsewhere.

The loss is presented as a simple, parameter-free alternative to standard likelihood training. Theoretical insights and experiments across model scales and challenging benchmarks support improved reasoning generalization. The finding concerns how strongly demonstrations should shape training: some difficult-to-fit wording deserves less influence when exact phrasing is not what determines whether the reasoning succeeds. It does not imply that every low-probability token is unimportant.
icml-2026-dont-force-the-fit-bounded-log.tldr: Bounded Log-Likelihood Loss limits the training influence of low-probability demonstration tokens, improving reasoning generalization in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: Graph learning often assumes that training labels are trustworthy, although real datasets can contain mislabeled nodes. The paper identifies two connected weaknesses in existing approaches: difficulty distinguishing dependable labels from unreliable ones, and insufficient use of relationships encoded by the graph. DREAM uses those relationships to guide how training handles labeled nodes.

During optimization, DREAM repeatedly reassesses each labeled node's reliability by comparing it with selected anchor nodes. Anchor selection follows two standards, considering both node proximity and graph topology. The method then measures semantic homogeneity between the target and its anchors, using their agreement as guidance for optimization. Reliability is therefore reconsidered as training progresses rather than assigned only once.

The authors provide theoretical analysis supporting this design and evaluate it on six graph datasets from different domains under three types of label noise. Comparisons with competing baselines demonstrate the method's effectiveness. The central contribution is to make label-noise handling responsive to both evolving training information and the relational structure that distinguishes graph data from isolated examples.
icml-2026-dream-dual-standard-semantic-h.tldr: DREAM repeatedly assesses noisy graph labels using semantic agreement with anchors selected through node proximity and graph topology.

paragraphs: Pose synchronization reconstructs absolute positions and orientations from noisy measurements of relative transformations. It is important in robotics and 3D vision, but conventional pipelines often use several heuristic steps to obtain valid poses. This paper formulates the problem directly with unit dual quaternions, a representation that combines rotation and translation.

The algorithm has two stages. A spectral initializer applies the power method to a Hermitian dual quaternion measurement matrix to obtain a starting estimate. A dual quaternion generalized power method then refines it, projecting each iteration back into the feasible set. Validity is thus enforced throughout refinement rather than left to a separate heuristic recovery procedure.

The paper establishes estimation-error bounds for spectral estimators and a finite-iteration bound for the refinement method. Its error contracts linearly until reaching an explicit threshold determined by noise; the guarantee does not promise unlimited improvement despite noisy measurements. Synthetic experiments and real multi-scan point-set registration show better accuracy and efficiency than representative matrix-based methods, connecting the theoretical formulation to practical pose recovery.
icml-2026-dual-quaternion-se-3-synchroni.tldr: A dual quaternion pose-synchronization algorithm combines efficient refinement with recovery bounds and linear error contraction down to a noise-dependent threshold.

paragraphs: Test-time reinforcement learning samples candidate answers and updates a model using provisional labels derived from majority votes. Tree-shaped sampling saves work by sharing reasoning prefixes, but uncertainty-driven branching can spend most of the budget on a few repeatedly uncertain paths. Early voting errors can also become self-reinforcing as the model updates toward unreliable answers.

ECHO addresses sampling and updating together. During sampling, it combines local entropy, a measure of uncertainty, with confidence assessed across a group to control how widely the tree branches. It also stops branches that remain low-confidence, reducing the chance that persistent uncertainty consumes the available exploration budget.

During updates, ECHO adjusts clipping according to confidence and combines entropy with confidence when shaping the learning signal. These mechanisms aim to reduce the influence of early biased labels while retaining exploration. Experiments report consistent improvements on mathematical and visual reasoning benchmarks and better generalization with limited rollout budgets. The findings support coordinating where a model explores with how strongly it learns from the resulting answers.
icml-2026-echo-entropy-confidence-hybrid.tldr: ECHO combines uncertainty and confidence to allocate reasoning branches and stabilize test-time reinforcement learning under limited sampling budgets.

paragraphs: Mixture-of-Experts models reduce computation by activating only selected expert components. Converting an existing dense language model into this form can avoid the expense of training an expert model from scratch. This paper argues that existing conversion methods disrupt useful activation patterns already present in dense models, weakening how they construct experts.

The authors examine Gated Linear Units and find a larger-scale organization within their neuron-level activity. Some neurons activate consistently across inputs, while others activate selectively. ExpertWeaver uses these patterns to divide neurons into shared experts and specialized experts chosen by routing, with configurations adapted to individual layers. The conversion framework itself requires no training.

Experiments show that ExpertWeaver outperforms existing methods in two roles: training-free dynamic structural pruning and initialization of highly sparse expert models through downcycling. The finding suggests that dense networks already contain useful clues about how to allocate shared and specialized computation. Preserving those clues gives conversion a structure grounded in the model's observed behavior.
icml-2026-expertweaver-unlocking-the-inh.tldr: ExpertWeaver converts dense language models into sparse expert structures by preserving universal and specialized neuron activation patterns.

paragraphs: Automatic modulation recognition identifies the modulation used in a signal. Learning useful representations with very few labeled examples is difficult when self-supervised transformations do not respect signal structure. The paper identifies ineffective direction-independent augmentations, spectral instability, and changes in semantic meaning as problems in standard self-supervised approaches.

DyCo-CL combines Virtual Adversarial Augmentation with a semantic consistency loss. The augmentation explores variations around signals, while the consistency term encourages their representations to retain meaning. The theoretical analysis indicates that this combination implicitly regularizes the encoder's spectral behavior, supporting more stable exploration of the representation manifold.

Two architectural components complement that objective. A signal-adaptive Swin backbone uses fixed attention windows to constrain locality, and a knowledge-fusion module incorporates physical priors into the representations. Experiments on RML benchmarks report a 6.27% accuracy gain over prior methods in one-shot settings. The result supports combining structure-aware transformations, semantic consistency, and physical knowledge when labeled examples are especially scarce.
icml-2026-geometry-aware-contrastive-lea.tldr: DyCo-CL combines geometry-aware augmentation, semantic consistency, and physical priors to improve modulation recognition with very few labeled examples.

paragraphs: Tree-based retrieval-augmented generation organizes source material into hierarchies so a model can retrieve broad summaries or specific details. Questions requiring evidence across documents expose weaknesses in existing designs: rigid clustering can introduce noise, separate trees can isolate related documents, and coarse summaries can hide information needed for a precise answer.

Ψ-RAG introduces a hierarchical abstract tree built through repeated merging and collapse. The construction adapts to the data distribution without a predetermined distributional assumption. A retrieval agent then works across levels of detail, reorganizing queries and using a hybrid retriever to interact with the knowledge base.

The framework supports tasks ranging from token-level question answering to document-level summarization. On cross-document questions requiring multiple reasoning steps, the paper reports average F1 improvements of 25.9% over RAPTOR and 7.4% over HippoRAG 2. These results support jointly improving the organization of evidence and the process used to retrieve it, particularly when an answer depends on connecting details spread across documents.
icml-2026-hierarchical-abstract-tree-for.tldr: Ψ-RAG combines an adaptive hierarchical index with multi-granular agent retrieval to improve question answering across documents.

paragraphs: Continuous-time reinforcement learning studies decisions in environments that evolve continuously, even though observations occur at selected times. This paper asks how learning performance can reflect the difficulty of a particular environment. It proposes a model-based algorithm using maximum likelihood estimation with a general function approximator.

The distinctive choice is to estimate the marginal distribution of states rather than directly estimate the system's dynamics. The analysis derives a regret bound, measuring accumulated performance shortfall, that depends on total reward variance and measurement resolution. These dependencies connect the guarantee to properties of the specific problem and to how finely the learner observes it.

The regret becomes independent of the particular measurement strategy when observation frequency adapts appropriately to problem complexity. That independence is conditional on the adaptation, rather than an unrestricted claim about all observation schedules. The algorithm also introduces randomized measurement timing to improve sample efficiency without increasing measurement cost. Together, the results suggest a route toward learners whose observation and learning behavior adjust to environmental difficulty.
icml-2026-instance-dependent-continuous-.tldr: The paper develops continuous-time reinforcement learning guarantees that adapt to problem difficulty through state-density estimation and measurement scheduling.

paragraphs: Generating a 3D mesh requires specifying both where vertices lie and how they connect. LATO introduces a structured latent representation intended to preserve this topology while supporting scalable generation. It represents a mesh through a surface-anchored Vertex Displacement Field and compresses that signal with a sparse voxel variational autoencoder.

Decoding progressively subdivides and prunes voxels to recover precise vertex locations. A dedicated connection head then queries the latent representation to predict edges between pairs of vertices. Because connectivity is predicted directly, the pipeline recovers mesh topology without extracting an isosurface or applying heuristic meshing procedures.

Generation uses two stages of flow matching: first creating the structure voxels, then refining topology features within those voxels. The authors report that LATO produces complex geometry and well-formed topology with efficient inference compared with prior isosurface-based or triangle-based diffusion models and autoregressive approaches. The key contribution is a representation that keeps geometric placement and connectivity accessible throughout compression, generation, and reconstruction.
icml-2026-lato-3d-mesh-flow-matching-wit.tldr: LATO generates explicit 3D meshes through structured voxel latents that support direct prediction of vertex positions and connectivity.

paragraphs: One-class audio deepfake detection learns the characteristics of genuine speech and rejects recordings that fall outside them. Its central difficulty is defining a sufficiently tight acceptance region without training on spoof examples. The paper argues that introducing auxiliary negatives can orient the boundary toward familiar artifacts and weaken generalization to unseen attacks.

CA-SOADD constructs off-manifold boundary probes to refine that region while retaining real-only training. Its centroid-anchored learning objective encourages genuine examples to remain compact and imposes a centroid-referenced margin against the probes. The probes help shape the boundary without being treated as an explicit negative class. Domain-conditioned centroids extend the approach to heterogeneous data settings.

Experiments on ASVSpoof and MLAAD show consistent improvements over strong baselines under unseen attack types and domain shifts, with ablations supporting the framework's effectiveness. The contribution is a way to tighten acceptance around genuine speech without relying on labeled spoof examples. This directly addresses the tension between learning a useful rejection boundary and avoiding dependence on already encountered attack artifacts.
icml-2026-learning-tight-rejection-bound.tldr: CA-SOADD uses centroid-based constraints and boundary probes to improve audio deepfake detection while training strictly on real speech.

paragraphs: Flow matching models generate samples through iterative numerical integration, which can make them expensive for real-time use. Distillation aims to compress that process into fewer steps. This paper argues that methods borrowed from diffusion-based score matching can overlook flow geometry and suffer from unstable training, noisy optimization signals, and reduced generation quality.

Mean Flow Distillation builds the distillation objective around average flow behavior. The theoretical analysis describes it as a temporal low-pass filter: it suppresses rapidly varying optimization noise associated with variational score distillation while maintaining consistency across the full trajectory. The Mean Flow Matching Theorem further establishes that matching expected average velocities is sufficient for strict distribution alignment.

That theorem provides a sufficient route to alignment, without claiming that average-velocity matching is the only possible route. Empirical evaluations cover 4D occupancy forecasting and text-to-image generation on high-dimensional manifolds. The authors report state-of-the-art performance and high-fidelity generation in a single step, supporting flow-specific distillation as a way to combine faster sampling with more stable optimization.
icml-2026-mean-flow-distillation-robust-.tldr: Mean Flow Distillation uses average flow velocities to stabilize distillation and enable high-fidelity single-step generation.

paragraphs: Solving geometry problems often requires selecting several theorems in a useful order. This paper explores doing so through in-context learning without additional gradient-based training. It identifies Structural Drift: as reasoning gets deeper, ordinary in-context learning degrades because the language model struggles to recover dependencies between reasoning steps and explores without enough structure.

The proposed Theorem Precedence Graphs encode temporal dependencies from historical solution traces as directed connections. These graphs constrain which reasoning paths are explored during inference. Retrieval helps construct the relevant graph, while a stepwise symbolic executor works alongside the language model, allowing it to function as a planner within an explicitly structured search process.

On FormalGeo7k, the method achieves 89.29% accuracy, substantially exceeding in-context learning baselines and matching state-of-the-art supervised models. The finding supports using explicit structural information to guide multi-step theorem prediction without updating model parameters. Historical solutions contribute more than examples to imitate: their ordering relationships become constraints that help organize subsequent reasoning.
icml-2026-non-parametric-structural-prio.tldr: Theorem Precedence Graphs guide training-free geometry reasoning with explicit dependencies, achieving 89.29% accuracy on FormalGeo7k.

paragraphs: Diffusion Transformers can generate detailed images, but training directly at very high resolutions is costly. This paper studies how to extend generation to larger images at inference time. It argues that applying the same positional-modulation schedule at every resolution overlooks how image scale changes the denoising process.

At higher resolution, a fixed semantic pattern occupies lower normalized spatial frequencies, while global structure must be coordinated over a larger spatial region. Structural stabilization therefore happens later. Ending guidance too early can disrupt the global layout, whereas carrying excessive intervention into late denoising can damage texture. The timing must accommodate both effects.

SigMa uses sigmoid modulation with two scaling laws, Decoupled Geometric Center Alignment and Iso-Variance Rate Adaptation, to make extrapolation scale-adaptive without additional training. Experiments demonstrate extrapolation up to 16 megapixels and best or competitive performance among the tested training-free baselines. The result supports adjusting the modulation schedule to target resolution so that global structure and local texture receive intervention at more appropriate stages.
icml-2026-sigmoid-modulation-for-ultra-h.tldr: SigMa adapts diffusion positional modulation to image scale, enabling training-free extrapolation up to 16 megapixels.

paragraphs: Slot Attention groups image features into object-level representations by repeatedly refining query slots. For an image or the first video frame, those queries begin without information specific to the input. Later video frames are different: their queries inherit information from previous slots. The paper argues that these distinct starting conditions call for different aggregation behavior.

SmoothSA first prepares cold-start queries using rich input-feature information. A small module, trained through self-distillation within the object-centric learning system, supplies this preparation. For video, the method then uses the full set of refinement iterations on the first frame and a single iteration on subsequent frames, reflecting their already informed starting points.

Experiments on object discovery, recognition, and visual reasoning validate the method's effectiveness, and visual analyses examine its mechanisms. The contribution is to adjust both initialization and recurrence to the information already available. Better prepared initial queries address the first-frame difficulty, while differentiated iteration schedules address the transition to frames that already have object-specific context.
icml-2026-smoothing-slot-attention-itera.tldr: SmoothSA prepares Slot Attention queries with input features and uses different refinement schedules for initial and subsequent video frames.

paragraphs: A unified medical model can both understand multimodal inputs and generate images, but placing those capabilities in one system does not automatically make them help each other. SynerMedGen asks which understanding objectives actually benefit generation. Its central principle is to align understanding tasks with the requirements of medical image synthesis.

The framework introduces three generation-aligned understanding tasks and a two-stage training strategy. Representations learned during understanding training are transferred into image synthesis. This makes the relationship between the tasks functional: the understanding phase is designed to develop information that the generation phase can use.

The authors report strong zero-shot results across 22 medical image synthesis tasks even after understanding training alone, together with robust generalization. Adding generation training yields consistent improvements over state-of-the-art specialized synthesis models and recent unified medical models. They also release SynerMed, containing one million paired synthesis samples and two million understanding instances. The findings support choosing understanding objectives for their relevance to generation when building unified medical models.
icml-2026-synermedgen-synergizing-medica.tldr: SynerMedGen aligns medical understanding tasks with image synthesis, allowing understanding training to improve generation and zero-shot performance.

paragraphs: Generative robot policies can produce different plausible actions, but single-shot inference commits to just one output. TapSampling explores improving control by spending additional computation when selecting an action. Its plug-and-play framework generates multiple candidates and evaluates them according to predicted progress toward the task.

An Action-VAE maps policy-generated initial actions into a compressed posterior distribution in a low-dimensional latent space. Samples from that distribution are decoded into candidate actions that approximate the true action distribution. A separate verifier predicts task-progress outcomes, using the sequential structure of robotic datasets for training. This grounds action selection in an interpretable notion of progress.

The framework is policy-agnostic, and experiments in simulation and real-world environments show substantial improvements for multiple generalist policies without further policy fine-tuning. The finding demonstrates an additional route to better control beyond increasing policy size or training data. A policy's initial output becomes the basis for candidate exploration, while the verifier helps choose among the resulting possibilities.
icml-2026-tapsampling-inference-time-sam.tldr: TapSampling improves robotic policies at inference time by sampling candidate actions and selecting them with a task-progress verifier.

paragraphs: An optimizer may avoid needing exact problem parameters yet still require a valid upper or lower bound on them. This paper calls such methods partially parameter-free. Its stronger goal is to remove algorithmic input requirements that depend on unverifiable conditions about the true problem parameters, while retaining convergence competitive with well-tuned methods.

GRASP approaches this through a general grid-search framework and a self-bounding analysis that determines parameter search ranges. Choosing those ranges is central: a search is not fully free of hidden parameter knowledge if its boundaries must already be supplied correctly. The analysis is designed to address that dependency.

For non-convex problems, the authors establish a fully parameter-free method with a near-optimal convergence rate up to logarithmic factors. For convex problems, they report competitive guarantees involving acceleration and universality. They also sharpen the guarantee for the model-ensemble step under an interpolated variance characterization. The contribution is both an optimization framework and an analysis of how search can avoid relying on unverifiable prior bounds.
icml-2026-towards-fully-parameter-free-s.tldr: GRASP uses grid search and self-bounding analysis to pursue strong optimization guarantees without unverifiable prior bounds on problem parameters.

paragraphs: Compressing a language model's weights to three values can reduce storage and computation, but high-precision activations can still limit inference speed. Activation outliers make lowering their precision difficult. TWLA is a post-training quantization framework that addresses weights and activations together, targeting 1.58-bit weights and 4-bit activations while maintaining high accuracy.

Its ternary quantizer minimizes layer-output error through an initial Euclidean optimization followed by manifold relocation. A structured orthogonal rotation reshapes weights toward three clusters suitable for ternarization and statistically suppresses activation outliers. These components make the model's numerical distributions more compatible with the desired precision.

A third component allocates activation precision using interactions between adjacent layers and differences in how much individual layers benefit from quantization after rotation. This is intended to prevent a few vulnerable layers from triggering cascading errors. Experiments report high accuracy under the W1.58A4 configuration alongside significant inference acceleration. The contribution is a coordinated treatment of weight compression, activation outliers, and cross-layer sensitivity rather than weight ternarization alone.
icml-2026-twla-achieving-ternary-weights.tldr: TWLA combines ternary weight quantization, distribution-shaping rotations, and layer-aware activation precision to accelerate language-model inference while maintaining high accuracy.
